Eight bytes walk into a bar.
The bartender asks, "Can I get you anything?"
"Yeah," reply the bytes.
"Make us a double."

idiom.title: Actions Speak Louder Than Words
idiom.interpretationEn: This phrase originates from 16th-century England, and it means that actions are a more powerful demonstration of one’s intentions and feelings than words. It reminds people not to rely solely on what others say but to look at what they do to truly understand their intentions.
idiom.interpretationZh: 这个短语起源于 16 世纪的英国，意指实际行动比言辞更能表达一个人的真实意图和感受。它提醒人们不要仅仅依赖言辞，而是要通过实际行动来证明自己。

examples.en: He keeps promising to help, but actions speak louder than words; so far, he hasn’t done anything.
examples.zh: 他说了很多次要帮忙，但行动胜于言辞，到目前为止他什么都没做。

examples.en: She says she loves him, but since actions speak louder than words, she’s planning a surprise for him this weekend.
examples.zh: 她说她爱他，但因为行动胜于言辞，她正在计划这个周末给他一个惊喜。

examples.en: In politics, actions speak louder than words; politicians need to show their commitment through their deeds.
examples.zh: 在政治中，行动胜于言辞：政治家需要通过他们的作为来展示他们的承诺。

people.name: Sophie Magdalene of Brandenburg-Kulmbach
people.bio: Queen of Denmark and Norway from 1730 to 1746
people.extract: Sophie Magdalene of Brandenburg-Kulmbach was Queen of Denmark and Norway by marriage to King Christian VI of Denmark and Norway.

people.name: Margaret Tudor
people.extract: Margaret Tudor was Queen of Scotland from 1503 until 1513 as the wife of James IV. She then served as regent of Scotland during her son's minority, and fought to extend her regency. Margaret was the eldest daughter of Henry VII of England and Elizabeth of York, and the elder sister of Henry VIII. Through her descendants, the House of Stuart eventually acceded to the thrones of England and Ireland, culminating in the "Union of the Crowns" under her great-grandson James VI and I in 1603 following the death of her niece Elizabeth I.

people.name: Rose Bampton
people.extract: Rose Bampton was an American opera singer who had an active international career during the 1930s and 1940s. She began her professional career performing mostly minor roles from the mezzo-soprano repertoire in 1929 but later switched to singing primarily leading soprano roles in 1937 until her retirement from the opera stage in 1963.
